objective: Open primary sources on LLM-driven formulaic alpha mining with out-of-sample decay evidence (AlphaAgent, R&D-Agent(Q), Alpha-GPT), then verify and cite an economically-grounded, diverse set of academic sources backing each of the 8 preregistered Claude-authored factors, before any IC is computed.

sources.core_claim: AlphaAgent's LLM-driven formulaic-alpha loop achieves S&P 500 test-window IC 0.0056 / ICIR 0.0552 (2021-2025), about a quarter of its own China CSI 500 IC (0.0212) for the identical method and LLM backend.
sources.project_applicability: Sets a realistic, not-optimistic U.S.-equity IC expectation band for judging this task's own batch.
sources.reflection: Verified via full-text curl snapshot and exact quote binding; the U.S.-market weakness relative to China is the single most important caution this prior-art check surfaced.

sources.core_claim: R&D-Agent(Q)'s NASDAQ 100 out-of-sample test (2024-01 to 2025-06-30, genuinely post-2023) beats classical factor libraries (Alpha158/360/AutoAlpha) by roughly 3.5-4x on IC (0.0162 vs 0.0040-0.0046).
sources.project_applicability: The closest existing precedent to this task's own decision rule (batch vs zoo on TEST IC), used to calibrate expectations, not copied as a target since the loop there is far heavier (multi-agent, bandit-scheduled, many iterations) than this task's single-revision 8+4 batch.
sources.reflection: Verified via full-text curl snapshot and exact quote binding on the disclosed train/validation/test date split and the NASDAQ100 results table.

sources.core_claim: Alpha-GPT is a human-in-the-loop LLM alpha-mining framework (prompt engineering + genetic-programming refinement); no post-2023 U.S. OOS IC/Sharpe table is disclosed at the abstract level.
sources.project_applicability: Completes the brief's named three-method sweep; contributes no usable performance number, only confirms the method's shape differs (human-in-the-loop, not autonomous batch) from this task's design.
sources.reflection: Abstract-only snapshot verified via curl; full PDF not opened this pass (no decay-evidence number to extract).

sources.core_claim: Cohen/Malloy/Pomorski (2012): opportunistic insider trades carry all the predictive power in the insider-trading universe (82bp/month abnormal return); routine trades (over half the universe) carry none.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds candidate F02 (opportunistic_insider_signal), directly operationalizing the opportunistic-vs-routine distinction the project's existing insider_cluster_buy card does not isolate.
sources.reflection: Verified via curl snapshot and abstract-text quote match.

sources.core_claim: Gervais/Kaniel/Mingelgrin (2001): stocks with unusually high (low) trading activity over a day/week tend to appreciate (depreciate) over the following month -- the 'high-volume return premium'.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds candidate F03 (trading_activity_surge): recent-vs-baseline trade-count ratio, a construct unused by any existing local card.
sources.reflection: Verified via curl snapshot and abstract-text quote match.

sources.core_claim: Christophe/Ferri/Hsieh (2010): abnormal short-selling precedes analyst downgrades, consistent with informed short sellers.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the informed-short-seller premise used by F01, F04 and F06.
sources.reflection: Verified via curl snapshot and abstract-text quote match.

sources.core_claim: Diether/Lee/Werner (2009): short sellers correctly predict future negative abnormal returns using 2005 SEC-mandated short-sale data.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds F04 (SUE + short-volume gate) and F06 (momentum + short-volume gate).
sources.reflection: Verified via full-PDF pdftotext snapshot and abstract-text quote match (author's own posted PDF, since the publisher's Oxford Academic page returned a bot-challenge page).

sources.core_claim: Chordia/Subrahmanyam/Anshuman (2001): variability (not just level) of trading activity is negatively related to expected returns, controlling for standard factors.
sources.project_applicability: Secondary support distinguishing the variability-of-activity mechanism from the level-of-activity premium F03 uses as its primary citation.
sources.reflection: RePEc landing page title/venue/year confirmed via curl snapshot; full abstract text not surfaced on that page, bibliographic facts cross-checked via web search of multiple citing sources rather than a second full-text read.

sources.core_claim: Ke/Huddart/Petroni (2003): insiders trade on private knowledge of forthcoming earnings disclosures up to two years ahead.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds F08 (earnings-recency-gated insider buying); note the paper's own tested direction is insider SELLING ahead of earnings declines, so the buying-after-good-news application here is our own extrapolation, disclosed and reflected in F08's lower (0.50) confidence score.
sources.reflection: RePEc landing page title/venue/year confirmed via curl snapshot; full abstract text not surfaced on that page, bibliographic facts cross-checked via web search of multiple citing sources rather than a second full-text read.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: A planned Round-1 factor (8-K filing-length/complexity, Loughran-McDonald-style) was dropped before preregistration once querying data/features/earnings_events showed it starts 2024-01-03, giving zero coverage of the SELECT window (2016-06-01..2023-12-29) -- it would have been unselectable by the SELECT-ICIR rule regardless of merit, not a fair test. Replaced with F03 (trading_activity_surge, daily_broad-based, full 2016+ coverage) before any IC was computed.

Sets expectations for this batch's likely IC magnitude to the AlphaAgent S&P500 order (roughly 0.005-0.01), not the higher China-market number, avoiding an inflated bar for judging 'supported vs refuted'.

F02 uses insider_broad's own opportunistic_buy_60d/routine_buy_60d columns (isolating the informative component) instead of re-running the project's existing buyer-count>=2 event rule, satisfying the brief's 'new element vs refuted mechanism' requirement for insider-cluster signals.
